discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman proposed using one quantum system to emulate another. Ultracold atoms in optical lattices made this a working experimental science. Zoller and co-workers showed in 1998 that atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, the first clean realisation of a strongly correlated lattice model with fully tunable parameters. The same programme went on to deliver single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes, which Greiner and Bloch pioneered. These instruments imaged Mott shells, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, many-body localization and entanglement entropy. Such questions are often beyond classical computation and beyond controlled theory. The work turned condensed-matter Hamiltonians into laboratory objects that can be measured atom by atom. It also laid the conceptual and technical groundwork for today's neutral-atom quantum processors.
